title: Design a Double-Entry Payment & Ledger System
prompt: Design a payment and ledger system (like Stripe or PayPal) processing 5,000 TPS where no dollar can ever be double-charged, lost, or created out of thin air—even across network retries and PSP timeouts.

Design a payment and ledger system (like Stripe or PayPal) processing 5,000 TPS where no dollar can ever be double-charged, lost, or created out of thin air—even across network retries and PSP.

The design partitions state, bounds tail latency, and isolates failure domains.

stages.title: Clarify invariants, idempotency & scale
stages.prompt: Every payment state transition must be backed by immutable double-entry ledger rows (debit + credit summing to 0) inside [ACID transactions](/concept/acid-transaction-fundamentals). Clients send a UUID `Idempotency-Key` so mobile network retries never charge a card twice.

keyInsights: Never mutate a single `balance` column without an append-only `ledger_entries` audit trail.
Store `idempotency_key` with a unique constraint in [PostgreSQL](/domains/sql) so duplicate retries return the original response.

tradeOffs.pro: Multi-row atomic debit+credit in one transaction

stages.title: Payment execution, PSP calls & Outbox
stages.prompt: Never hold a database transaction open while calling an external Payment Service Provider (Visa/Stripe). Instead, record `PENDING` locally, release the DB connection, call the PSP, and commit `SETTLED` + an outbox event for [Kafka](/domains/kafka) via the [Transactional Outbox](/concept/transactional-outbox-pattern).

keyInsights: Lock accounts in sorted `account_id` order (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`) to eliminate deadlocks.
Run nightly three-way reconciliation comparing internal ledger, PSP settlement files, and bank statements.

failureModes.name: PSP Timeout Ambiguity
failureModes.description: PSP charges the card, but the HTTP response times out before reaching your server.
failureModes.mitigation: Forward the idempotency key to the PSP and resolve `UNKNOWN` states via async webhook + polling reconciler.

putItTogether.title: Put the Payment Ledger together
putItTogether.summary: Combine idempotency keys at the API edge, immutable double-entry rows in [SQL](/domains/sql), out-of-transaction PSP calls, and CDC outbox publishing to [Kafka](/domains/kafka).
steps: Write immutable debit/credit pairs inside a short ACID transaction with sorted row locks.
Publish settlement events via Transactional Outbox + CDC.
putItTogether.outcome: Zero double-charges, zero lost money, and full cryptographic/accounting auditability.

questions.prompt: Why should you NEVER keep a database transaction open while calling an external payment gateway API?

options.text: It holds DB connections and row locks across unpredictable 2–30s network I/O, exhausting the pool and stalling other users
options.explanation: Correct! Keep DB transactions strictly local and transition through an explicit PENDING state.
The DB doesn't block HTTP, but holding locks/connections across slow external calls causes cascading pool exhaustion.

prerequisites.title: ACID Transaction Fundamentals
prerequisites.summary: ACID groups four guarantees for a database transaction: Atomicity (all-or-nothing), Consistency (enforced rules stay valid), Isolation (concurrent work does not expose partial state), and Durability (committed changes survive a crash under configured disk-flus...

prerequisites.title: Idempotency & Deduplication
prerequisites.summary: Idempotency keys and deduplication logs ensure that network retries, at-least-once message deliveries, and double-clicks execute state mutations at most once while returning the original cached outcome.

prerequisites.title: Transactional Outbox Pattern
prerequisites.summary: The Transactional Outbox pattern eliminates dual-write split-brain by inserting domain events into an `outbox` table inside the exact same ACID database transaction as the business state change, then relaying them asynchronously to Kafka/RabbitMQ.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Double-Entry Payment & Ledger System without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: When a single bottleneck threatens end-to-end availability, zero double-charges, zero lost money, and full cryptographic/accounting auditability.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

decisionExercise.prompt: When Design a Double-Entry Payment & Ledger System experiences a sudden 5x traffic spike alongside a slow downstream dependency, which engineering choice best protects system stability?

options.label: Increase retry counts and remove client timeouts so every request eventually succeeds.
options.explanation: Unbounded retries multiply load on an already struggling dependency and exhaust worker pools.

options.label: Enforce strict latency budgets, bounded jittered retries, and graceful fallback or load shedding.
options.explanation: Bounding retries and isolating slow paths preserves healthy capacity and keeps tail latency predictable.
